key_insight: The paper proves that random monitored Clifford circuits have a unique stationary distribution and shows that weak non-Clifford "magic" accumulates with different asymptotic laws depending on the resource measure and local dimension.
engineering_relevance: This provides a rigorous long-time model for measurement-aware quantum circuit behavior, useful for benchmarking error mitigation, resource injection, and hybrid Clifford/non-Clifford circuit design.
method: Proved existence and uniqueness of the stationary law for random monitored Clifford dynamics.
Analyzed the weak-magic-injection limit to derive leading-order steady-state scaling.
Compared resource geometry via Gross--Wigner mana (odd prime d) and 2-stabilizer Rényi entropy (qubits).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical results establishing ergodicity and asymptotic steady-state scaling, rather than numerical benchmarking or experimental data.
watch_item: The asymptotic laws are derived for a specific random monitored Clifford setting, so transfer to non-Clifford-dominated or finite-size practical circuits may require additional analysis.
paper_title: Invariant Measures and Weak-Magic-Injection Asymptotics in Random Monitored Quantum Circuits
